requirement: Give every aiohttp.web request a safe request id taken from X-Request-ID or generated, expose it to handlers and responses, and turn HTTP exceptions and crashes into JSON error bodies without leaking exception text.
skeleton: A header constant, an id pattern, and a web.middleware function choosing the id, calling the handler, mapping HTTPException and other exceptions to JSON responses, and setting the header.
caption: Request ids and JSON errors as aiohttp.web middleware. request_id_middleware, decorated with web.middleware, keeps an incoming X-Request-ID only when it fully matches 1 to 64 letters, digits or dashes, otherwise generates uuid4().hex, and stores it as request['request_id'] for handlers. It awaits the handler; a web.HTTPException becomes a JSON body with its reason and the request id under the exception's own status, and any other Exception is logged with logger.exception naming the id and becomes a generic 500 body saying internal server error, never the exception text. Every response, success or error, carries the X-Request-ID header. The fixture asserts, over an aiohttp TestServer, that abc-123 and a 64-character id are echoed to handler and header, that a spaced id, a 65-character id or no id get a fresh 32-hex id, that a RuntimeError is a 500 without its secret and is logged with the id, that HTTPForbidden keeps 403 and its reason, and that an unknown path is a JSON 404 Not Found.

plan.intent: Correlate logs and client errors without exposing internals
constraints: Incoming ids are kept only if they match 1 to 64 letters, digits or dashes
HTTPException keeps its status and reason in a JSON body
Unhandled exceptions are logged and answered with a generic JSON 500
X-Request-ID is set on every response

rationale.teaches: Validate client-supplied correlation ids, handle HTTPException separately from crashes in middleware, and log details server-side while returning generic errors.
rationale.why: Echoing arbitrary header values enables log injection, folding HTTPException into 500 breaks 403 and 404, and returning str(exc) leaks secrets.

ops.docstring: Request-id propagation and JSON error bodies as aiohttp.web middleware.

candidates.why_wrong: Ids longer than 32 characters are replaced even though up to 64 are allowed.
Any client header value, spaces and all, is trusted as the request id.
HTTP exceptions such as 403 and 404 are swallowed into generic 500 responses.
Generated ids use the dashed 36-character uuid form instead of the 32-hex form.
The 500 body echoes the exception text, leaking secrets to the client.
